title: Interlock availability ledger and handoff timeline
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an operational 'availability ledger' and a timeframe-driven handoff timeline that makes cross-team roadmap dependencies visible, actionable, and auditable. The ledger combines readiness signals (engineering capacity, infra slots, design artifacts, security approvals) with a deterministic handoff timeline so PMs can calculate cutover windows and contingency requirements. This ticket covers schema, UI surface in Console's Planning view, integration points with Linear/Slack/GitHub, and the runbook for escalation and mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger schema defined and approved by Eng/Design/Security/Infra
Console Planning view prototype that lists dependencies by initiative with readiness columns populated from team-owned signals
Automated weekly sync that aggregates readiness signals from Linear issues, Design Figma status, infra capacity API and security review tracker
Can simulate a cutover window and surface recommended contingency buckets (defer, scope-reduce, parallel migration)
Runbook for triage and 24/72 hour escalation steps documented and reviewed
tasks: Define ledger data model and minimal required signals (owner, status, ETA, blockers)
Design wireframes for the Planning view table + compact mobile card
Instrument readiness endpoints: Linear API query for issue states, Design 'File readiness' flag from Figma, Infra capacity / allocation API, Security review tracker export
Prototype backend ingestion pipeline (kafka job + aggregator) and store in Planning DB
Build front-end component in Console and add feature flag for rollout
Write runbook and slack escalation playbook; schedule cross-team dry run
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial kick-off. Agreed to focus on 3 source signals for MVP: Linear issue state, Figma 'Ready for dev' tag, infra pool allocation. Security to provide CSV export until tracker API is available.

2025-01-20 - Priya Natarajan: Engineering flagged two constraints: backend schema must support shifting ETAs and multiple owners per dependency. We'll build a small change-data-capture (CDC) pipeline to handle updates without full re-ingestion.

2025-01-28 - Marisol Vega: Design trade-off meeting. Chose a compact horizontal layout over nested detail panes to minimize cognitive load in weekly roadmap reviews. Shared wireframes: https://figma.com/file/abcd-availability-ledger
2025-02-03 - Daniel Ortiz: Infra capacity API prototype is ready. It returns per-cluster slot allocations and reservation windows. Endpoint: https://infra.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools
2025-02-10 - Security (Rowan Patel): Security will run a dry-run approval cadence. For MVP, security_review_required = true for initiatives touching private deployments.
2025-02-15 - Liam Chen: Backend prototype deployed to staging. Ingestion job pulls Linear states and Figma flags. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4217
2025-02-18 - Jonah Kim: Analytics events defined (ledger.view, dependency.change, cutover.simulate). Need to instrument before can run readiness dashboards.
notes:
Decisions and trade-offs: We will start with a push model where teams publish readiness signals (Linear + Figma) rather than attempting to infer readiness automatically from PR status. This reduces false positives and places ownership with teams. Contingency buckets: 1) Defer non-critical subfeatures, 2) Run partial rollout to hosted only, 3) Allocate emergency infra burst (costly).

Open questions:
- Should SLA mappings be surfaced in ledger rows (TBD with SRE)?
- How to represent transitive dependencies concisely when depth >2? Proposal: show immediate upstream and allow expand on demand.

Next steps:
- Complete backend ingestion for Security CSV import (due 2025-02-24).
- Finish Console prototype and schedule cross-team dry run (target 2025-02-28).
- Run cadence: Weekly readiness sync email and Monday 30-minute alignment for owners.
